_comment: The docs' demos (record.py writes a GIF, an MP4 and a WebM each). `scenes` are scripted model replies like scripts/screenshots/scenes.json, kept short so each GIF fits in 15 s; the demo stack loads this file first, then scenes.json, so a demo can also use a screenshot scene. `demos` are the recordings: each one's steps run in order (record.py's Demo methods say what each step does). A wait on a running command may set `show_ms`: it plays faster to fit, so the runner's speed never sets the demo's length. The tile-* demos are the README's feature tiles: one feature each, on a task a user would really give, in the same window as the rest. A demo a README tile plays sets `cover_ms`: it opens on its cover for that long, then plays from the start, so a still of the tile (and its poster, the GIF's first frame) already shows the feature. The cover is the frame a `cover` step marks, else the last.

scenes.match: Write the changelog entry for the hourly view

steps.say:
Here's the entry.

**Hourly forecast.** The day screen now has an hourly strip: temperature, rain chance and wind for the next 24 hours. Tap an hour to see its details.

**Faster startup.** Forecasts are cached for ten minutes, so the app opens on the last forecast at once and refreshes in the background.

**Fixed:** wind speed follows the unit setting again.

scenes.match: Draft a note to the team about the hourly view

steps.say:
Here's a draft.

Hi all, the hourly view is ready to try on staging. The day screen now shows an hourly strip with temperature, rain chance and wind for the next 24 hours, and a tap on an hour opens its details.

What to check: the strip on a small phone, the units setting, and the first launch with no network. Please send anything odd to the release thread by Thursday, so we can ship to the app store next week.

steps.say: Done: `.github/workflows/checks.yml` runs the checks on every push.
Refreshing the cache from the forecast API.

args.command: cd forecast && sleep 7 && echo cache refreshed
args.title: Refresh the forecast cache

steps.say: The cache is fresh: 24 hours for each saved place.
You're on main. It's the only branch so far.
Checking the API log first.
It can't write to its cache. Checking how full the cache is.

The cache volume is full. Hourly snapshots have piled up for ten days, over 1 GB on a 1 GB volume, so the API can't save new forecasts and the proxy turns that into 502s. Deleting the old snapshots will fix it. Want me to do that?
Here's what's taking the space.
Deleting snapshots older than two days.
Done: the cache is down to about 200 MB, and the API can save new forecasts again.
Two changes went in this week. One reviewer for the cache change:

args.task: Review the forecast cache change (src/forecast/cache.py, "Cache forecasts for ten minutes") for bugs before the release. Report anything that should block it.
args.label: Review: cache

steps.say: And one for the wind speed fix:

args.task: Review the wind speed fix (src/forecast/units.py, "Fix wind speed ignoring the km/h setting") for bugs before the release. Report anything that should block it.
args.label: Review: wind speed fix

steps.say: Two reviewers are on it, one per change. I'll sum up when both report back.
The cache review is back: nothing blocking. Old keys are never evicted, so I'd cap the cache after the release.
The wind speed review is back too: nothing blocking.
Both reviews are in and nothing blocks the release: fine to tag.
Nothing blocking. Entries expire after 600 seconds as intended. Old keys are never removed, so memory grows with every place looked up; fine at today's size, worth a cap later.

args.command: cd forecast && git show --format=%s HEAD~2 -- src/forecast/units.py | tail -4
args.title: Read the fix

steps.say: Nothing blocking. km/h and mph are now right. A unit other than those two returns the raw m/s value without a warning; worth rejecting unknown units later.
